topic-032-taylor-expansion-of-discount-f.evolution: Early representatives study recurrence detection, control scheduling, and neural sequential decisions. Later work develops data-efficient model-based search and improved critic learning. Recent analyses move beyond linear MDP assumptions and examine low-rank structure, policy generalization, and linear filters that recover useful hidden-state information under specified transition conditions.
openQuestions: Which structural assumptions are testable before expensive interaction?
How can representation guarantees survive imperfect models and changing dynamics?
topic-032-taylor-expansion-of-discount-f.overview: Reinforcement learning must improve a policy from limited interaction while representing values, dynamics, or memory well enough to guide decisions. This cluster brings together model-based policy search, actor–critic methods, approximate policy iteration, and structural conditions for learnability. The focus is on what makes a useful decision representation possible beyond a small tabular environment.
topic-032-taylor-expansion-of-discount-f.title: Sample-Efficient Policy Learning and Control
topic-032-taylor-expansion-of-discount-f.whyItMatters: Large continuous state spaces can hide problems that are statistically impossible without additional structure. Explicit conditions help explain when nonlinear policies or compact recurrent memories can learn efficiently rather than merely succeed on selected benchmarks.

topic-033-2d-shapley-a-framework-for-fra.evolution: Earlier examples involve economic decisions and online mechanisms. Recent work analyzes strategic responses to fairness interventions and competitive collaboration, including mechanisms that restore honest updates. The newest representatives extend incentive questions to policy allocation and natural-language persuasion, while uncertainty about participant costs complicates robust strategic classification.
openQuestions: How can incentive guarantees remain useful when participants’ costs and objectives are only partly known?
Which learning improvements persist after people adapt to the deployed system?
topic-033-2d-shapley-a-framework-for-fra.overview: Learning systems interact with people or organizations that may change behavior in response to their rules. This topic studies strategic classification, collaborative learning, mechanism design, and information design. Instead of treating manipulation as arbitrary noise, the models examine what rational participants gain from reporting, withholding, or changing information.
topic-033-2d-shapley-a-framework-for-fra.title: Strategic Learning and Incentive Design
topic-033-2d-shapley-a-framework-for-fra.whyItMatters: An accurate predictor can create incentives that undermine its own data or intended policy. Designing rewards and communication rules jointly with learning can make honest participation compatible with good outcomes.

topic-034-a-character-level-length-contr.evolution: Earlier representatives concern discriminative parsing, translation, and probabilistic language modeling. The 2019–2022 work emphasizes masked sequence generation, multilingual reconstruction, and large-scale retrieval. Recent papers study continuous latent generation and tokenizer behavior, including efficient language identification derived from probabilistic token models.
openQuestions: Which pretraining objectives transfer reliably across both languages and generation tasks?
How should tokenizer quality be evaluated beyond average sequence length?
topic-034-a-character-level-length-contr.overview: Language models depend on how text is represented, what prediction task supplies training signals, and how generation is evaluated. This cluster includes sequence-to-sequence pretraining, paraphrasing, retrieval augmentation, translation, and tokenizer analysis. Several methods learn reusable structure by reconstructing text from related or partially observed language rather than treating every downstream task separately.
topic-034-a-character-level-length-contr.title: Language Pretraining, Sequence Generation, and Tokenization
topic-034-a-character-level-length-contr.whyItMatters: Choices made before fine-tuning can determine data efficiency, multilingual coverage, and the quality of generated text. Tokenization also affects what information a model can represent economically and how languages are distinguished.

topic-035-texttt-g1-teaching-llms-to-rea.evolution: Early representatives connect neural architectures to graph kernels and transferable relational structures. Later graph Transformers use rooted subgraph representations and integrate textual nodes. Recent language-model approaches encode graph distance alongside token position and adjust structural attention inside decoder-only models, seeking reasoning that respects both graph connectivity and causal generation order.
openQuestions: How can attention distinguish meaningful structural differences from graph symmetries?
Which graph encodings generalize to unseen topologies without task-specific retraining?
topic-035-texttt-g1-teaching-llms-to-rea.overview: Graph representations encode relationships that ordinary token order may obscure. This topic studies how attention models can preserve topology, structural similarity, and multi-hop connections while retaining flexible long-range computation. Methods combine graph encoders with Transformers or incorporate graph structure directly into attention and positional geometry.
topic-035-texttt-g1-teaching-llms-to-rea.title: Graph-Aware Attention and Language Models
topic-035-texttt-g1-teaching-llms-to-rea.whyItMatters: A sequence representation of a graph can lose important relationships or introduce arbitrary ordering effects. Structural information must influence actual computation, not merely appear as a decorative positional feature.

topic-036-3d-focusing-and-matching-netwo.evolution: The collection begins with point-cloud kernels and scene labeling, followed by hierarchical point-set networks. Later work adds few-shot detection, densification, and in-context understanding. Recent examples distill rotation-invariant synthetic data, tune topology-aware prompts, and use parallel transport to compare geometrically aligned features across domains.
openQuestions: How can one encoder remain reliable across sensors, densities, and coordinate conventions?
What information must synthetic point clouds preserve to transfer between architectures?
topic-036-3d-focusing-and-matching-netwo.overview: Point clouds describe shape without a fixed image grid, so models must handle unordered samples, changing resolution, and spatial transformations. This cluster studies hierarchical features, self-supervision, detection, data distillation, and adaptable encoders for 3D inputs. Geometry-aware attention extends the same questions to features defined in different local coordinate systems.
topic-036-3d-focusing-and-matching-netwo.title: Geometric Learning on Point Clouds
topic-036-3d-focusing-and-matching-netwo.whyItMatters: A representation that depends on arbitrary point order or orientation can fail despite observing the same object. Efficient learning must preserve shape information while accommodating sparse measurements and heterogeneous acquisition conditions.

topic-037-a-dynamic-algorithm-for-weight.evolution: Early representatives develop incremental and online utility maximization. Later work improves streaming efficiency and extends beyond simple cardinality constraints. Recent studies estimate instance-specific solution quality and connect sequential data selection to utility curvature, using submodular surrogates to make selection scalable and theoretically interpretable.
openQuestions: When does a learned utility retain enough submodular structure for reliable guarantees?
Can instance-specific certificates remain useful as the dataset changes?
topic-037-a-dynamic-algorithm-for-weight.overview: Submodular objectives model diminishing returns, making them useful for selecting diverse, representative subsets. These papers study greedy approximations, streaming and dynamic algorithms, nonmonotone objectives, and instance-specific guarantees. Related data-valuation work asks how a score for an item should reflect its contribution to an entire selection sequence.
topic-037-a-dynamic-algorithm-for-weight.title: Submodular Optimization and Data Selection
topic-037-a-dynamic-algorithm-for-weight.whyItMatters: The value of an example or resource depends on what has already been chosen. Treating every item independently can waste a budget on redundancy, while worst-case approximation ratios may understate performance on actual instances.

topic-038-boosting-a-positive-data-only-.evolution: Early representatives explore noisy classification and ensemble training. The 2000s work sharpens convergence and margin analyses while identifying limitations of convex boosting under noise. Recent studies quantify multiclass weak-learning costs, improve agnostic sample efficiency, and decompose errors in selective classification and boosted regression inference.
openQuestions: How can boosting tolerate realistic label noise without demanding an unrealistically strong weak learner?
Which scores correctly rank prediction reliability under distribution shift?
topic-038-boosting-a-positive-data-only-.overview: Boosting combines imperfect predictors into a stronger classifier, but its success depends on the weak learner, loss, noise model, and number of classes. This cluster studies margins, agnostic learning, cost-sensitive formulations, and statistical guarantees. Related reliability work examines how confidence rankings affect a classifier’s ability to abstain appropriately.
topic-038-boosting-a-positive-data-only-.title: Boosting, Weak Learning, and Classification Guarantees
topic-038-boosting-a-positive-data-only-.whyItMatters: Repeatedly improving a training objective does not guarantee robustness to noisy labels or efficient multiclass learning. Resource requirements can shift from the booster to its underlying learner, and confidence rescaling alone may not fix an incorrect ranking of predictions.

topic-039-nearly-efficient-algorithms-fo.evolution: Early representatives investigate discrete relaxation for graph matching. Later work develops distributed allocation, learned advice, and sharper stochastic guarantees. Recent studies address ties, calibration, and dynamic coarsening; a heart-transplant simulation illustrates how grouping resources can yield strong performance under an explicit model rather than merely simplifying the problem heuristically.
openQuestions: Which learned predictions improve matching when their errors are systematic?
How can allocation guarantees account for fairness and strategic responses as well as efficiency?
topic-039-nearly-efficient-algorithms-fo.overview: Matching algorithms pair participants or resources while respecting feasibility, preferences, and timing. This topic includes online and stochastic matching, stable matching, graph correspondence, and learning-augmented algorithms. Data can guide dual variables, predictions, or aggregation strategies, but the resulting allocation still needs a meaningful quality guarantee.
topic-039-nearly-efficient-algorithms-fo.title: Matching and Allocation with Learned Structure
topic-039-nearly-efficient-algorithms-fo.whyItMatters: Decisions often arrive before future requests are known, and a locally attractive match can consume a resource needed later. Structural information can improve practical allocation without assuming an omniscient view of the entire sequence.
